procedure.description: insertion of spinal neurostimulator pulse generator with connection to leads

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 63685 (insertion of spinal neurostimulator pulse generator with connection to leads) with date of service 2026-02-03. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish a successful trial meeting the plan’s definition of 50 percent pain reduction with functional improvement.

criteria.text: Chronic intractable neuropathic pain of the trunk or limbs (such as failed back surgery syndrome or complex regional pain syndrome) for at least 6 months despite conservative therapy including medications, physical therapy, and injections.
Psychological evaluation documenting no untreated psychiatric condition or substance use disorder that would preclude benefit from neuromodulation.
A successful trial of at least 5 days with at least 50 percent pain reduction and documented functional improvement.
No further surgically correctable lesion identified on imaging.

chart.text: Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

64 year old man in the pain clinic referred by his spine surgeon. Discussed spinal cord stimulation, what a trial involves, and that it is for leg-predominant neuropathic pain. He is interested. His history otherwise: seasonal allergies, migraines, rare now, anxiety, sees a counselor. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works as a teacher. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Persistent bilateral leg and low back pain 22 months after an L4-S1 fusion, 8 out of 10 most days, burning quality down both legs. On gabapentin 1200 three times daily and duloxetine 60, 18 weeks of PT, two epidurals and a medial branch block without durable relief. Post-operative MRI and CT show a solid fusion, no recurrent stenosis, no hardware problem; the spine surgeon has nothing further to offer surgically.

Psychological evaluation for neuromodulation candidacy. PHQ-9 score 10, mild; no somatic symptom disorder; no substance use disorder, opioid use stable and monitored; realistic expectations about pain reduction rather than cure. Cleared for trial.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Reviewed the psychological evaluation. Scheduling the trial. Anticoagulation and infection precautions reviewed. Vitals today 119 over 75, pulse 73.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.1, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 215, LDL 125, HDL 57, triglycerides 123. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
Percutaneous trial leads placed at T8 and T9 under fluoroscopy, paresthesia coverage of both legs and the low back confirmed. Trial programmed, home with the diary.

Trial day 5: pain down from 8 out of 10 to 3 out of 10, a 62 percent reduction. Walking 30 minutes a day, sleeping through the night, cut the oxycodone in half. Successful trial; proceed to permanent implant. Leads removed.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Mole on the right calf that his spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Blood pressure check. 142 over 83 today, 134 over 94 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Pre-op for permanent implant. Labs fine, nicotine negative. Consent signed for percutaneous leads and a rechargeable generator in the left upper buttock.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
